newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus international retail centre opens.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus international retail centre opens.

text.p: A $30 million international wholesale and exhibition centre opened its doors in Cyprus on Friday, hoping to woo clients in more than 50 countries with its "one-stop" buying facilities.

The International Merchandising Centre (IMC) is where businesses renting IMC space can sell their goods to overseas buyers at duty free prices, or to local clients with storage and delivery facilities readily available.

"It is one of the largest and most ambitious projects ever undertaken in Cyprus by the private sector to promote the country as a regional trade and business centre," said Kyriakos Christofi, the Cypriot Commerce and Industry Minister.

The project, financed by Arab Bank, the Cyprus Development Bank and Cypriot entrepreneur Andreas Kaisis, has drawn interest from the eastern Mediterranean, the Middle East, Russia and member-countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States.

The centre, on the outskirts of the capital Nicosia, consists of 22,000 square metres of exhibition space spread across five floors. Goods on display range from jewellery and fur coats to wooden kitchen panels from Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Africa.
IMC chairman Andreas Kaisis said future plans include a listing on the Cyprus stock exchange.

The IMC is also examining the possibility of creating a similar centre in Alexandroupolis, northern Greece, to attract business from the Balkans and Black Sea region in cooperation with the Hellenic Foreign Trade Board, he said.
